messages:
incident-bot: HIGH alert — GPU capacity exhaustion detected in us-west-2 (pool: gfx-prod-2). queue_length > 15k, avg latency spiking, autoscaler failed to exceed 220 nodes. paging on-call now. Details: https://grafana/redwood/d/abc123

jessica: acked. on-call here. seeing repeated CUDA/Xid errors in driver logs across ~12 nodes, and 5 nodes flapped in last 10m. autoscaler logs show 'scale_limit_reached' and frequent OOM kill on runtime.

raj: copying logs to thread. here's tail from runtime-driver on node gpu-148:
```
[2026-03-15T12:04:22Z] CUDA:Xid(37) context_abort
[2026-03-15T12:04:23Z] process pid=4412 killed, reason=OOM
[2026-03-15T12:05:01Z] node health: RESTARTING
```

liam: metrics: kernel_xid_rate per-node jumped from 0.1 -> 4.2 in 8m. queue growth is mostly from long-running batched requests (seq_len spikes). autoscaler config: max_nodes=220, currently at 220. attempted scale to 240 but rejected by quota API.

ops-sre: running immediate mitigations: 1) throttle non-critical routes via gateway 2) enable fallback to smaller model for PLG customers 3) move critical customers to warm reserved pool if possible. starting throttle now.

jessica: throttle applied to /v1/generate for 'free-tier' and 'exploratory' tags. API 429s should reduce ingest. can we also trigger drain of the 5 flapping nodes?

infra-lead: yes — prepping driver hotpatch but it's a bit risky. recommend cordon+drain flappers first. commands I ran: `kubectl cordon gpu-148 && kubectl drain gpu-148 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` — one node restarted and rejoined but still shows kernel Xid spikes.

ben: if autoscaler hit quota we need immediate capacity. can we request temporary quota bump? cloud-ops is paged. emailing oncall@cloudops now. meanwhile switching ~10 low-priority jobs to cpu-only fallback.

support-swift: heads up — customers with long-poll sessions may see degraded responses. alerting Support SRE and opening a status page note. impact: some inference requests delayed >5s, and a handful of customers seeing 500s. listing affected customers to PMs now.

raj: quick note — KV cache pressure increased; many ctx loads causing memory pressure on GPU processes. downgrading batch size on runtime to 1 for routes still helps reduce OOMs. pushing config: `RUNTIME_BATCH_SIZE=1` to prod-config.

liam: autoscaler behavior: it emits attempted_scale_to=240 at 12:07:11 but cloud quota API returned 403_quota_limit at 12:07:12. also saw repeated failures to attach new nodes due to driver init failing (Xid) causing immediate node eviction by kubelet. that loops and prevents effective scale.

ops-sre: short checklist for next 30m:
- keep throttle to non-prod routes
- move reserved pool capacity (reserved-pool-1) to handle top 5 paying customers
- cordon/drain nodes with Xid > 10 in last 5m
- apply runtime batch_size reduction globally for high-latency routes
- try rolling driver restart on a small subset with the hotpatch applied

jessica: support-swift — please prepare templated message to customers: short explain, mitigation in progress, ETA 60m for stabilization. be explicit about which endpoints affected.

support-swift: will do. drafting: "We're investigating increased latency and errors for generation endpoints in us-west-2. We've throttled exploratory traffic and are migrating critical workloads to reserved capacity. We'll provide updates every 30 minutes."

infra-lead: driver hotpatch ready (rdriver-2.3.7) — it includes a more graceful GPU memory reclaim and suppresses a known Xid trigger for our kernel version. plan: canary apply to 2 nodes, monitor 10m, then ramp. any objections?

ben: proceed with canary on nodes gpu-152 and gpu-153. ensure drain fallback if they misbehave.

raj: canary started at 12:23. gpu-152 shows reduced Xid rate so far (4 -> 0.6). no OOMs for 6m.

liam: autoscaler quota still pending. cloudops replied "temporary quota bump to 260 nodes approved for 2 hours" at 12:28. scaling to 240 now in progress.

ops-sre: after canary good, we'll roll patch to other flappers. also enabling a temporary policy to prefer nodes with driver-version >= 2.3.7 to routing decisions.

jessica: customer impact update: top 5 paying customers migrated to reserved-pool-1 at 12:30. latency for them dropped to baseline. PLG traffic still throttled.

support-swift: status page updated: "Mitigations in progress, some rate limiting applied. Expected stabilization within 60 minutes."

oncall-next: taking over page at 12:47. summary for next oncall:
- incident: GPU capacity exhaustion + autoscaler quota block + driver Xid/OOM causing node flaps
- actions done: throttle non-prod, reserved migration for top 5, canary driver patch applied and looks promising, quota bump requested and partly approved
- outstanding: complete driver rollout to remaining flappers, confirm autoscaler continues scaling to 240+, monitor queue_length < 2000, follow up with cloudops for extended quota if needed
- logs/links: https://grafana/redwood/d/abc123  https://logs.redwood/streams/grad-index?query=gpu

jessica: handing off to oncall-next. I'm available if needed.

oncall-next: ack — taking it. will post updates every 20m or on major change.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity -> degraded; mitigation in progress; next automated check in 15m."
